relevance.rationale: Lecture notes on quantum complexity and black holes: the complexity/entropy analogy, a second law of complexity, complexity growth as the black-hole interior's volume growth, firewalls as periods of non-increasing complexity, and 'uncomplexity' as a computational resource. rem:p-vs-np-event-horizon opens by claiming to 'formally establish a structural identity between computational complexity and jet horizon information loss', reformulating P vs NP as a horizon boundary condition, and cites nothing -- while an established research programme identifying computational complexity with black-hole horizon geometry exists and is exactly what this document reviews. That is a scholarly-positioning gap, not a mathematical one: nothing in the corpus block is wrong, and this document supplies no lemma the corpus consumes, so it is supporting rather than core. The value is that a referee will ask 'how does this relate to the complexity/horizon literature?' and the block currently has no answer. Note also that the two 'complexities' are not the same object -- the corpus's is worst-case circuit/time complexity of NP-complete decision problems, the document's is minimal-circuit-size complexity of a quantum state -- so any citation must position, not equate.

keyResults.locator: Lecture II (second law of complexity and the black-hole interior)
keyResults.statement: Quantum state complexity grows linearly for a time exponential in the entropy before saturating, and this growth is dual to the growth of the black-hole interior; non-increasing complexity is where firewall behaviour appears.
keyResults.useForFolio: Prior art for the complexity-equals-horizon-geometry identification that rem:p-vs-np-event-horizon asserts as its own structural identity; citing it lets the block state what is new in its version.

proposedActions.rationale: The block asserts a complexity-horizon structural identity with zero prior-art citation; the reference is the minimum needed to position the claim.
